title: Can an AI tell the difference between an attack near a shipping lane and a barrel of oil actually going missing?
author: thinq-81
selftext:
Traffic might continue. Insurance premiums might rise. Vessels might reroute and deliver the same cargo late. Each can affect a company’s costs, but they don’t all imply a lasting reduction in oil supply.

I built Market Ontology to connect geopolitical events to exposed positions. Open Analyst with a shipping headline and ask: “What physical flow has changed? What is the source? Which part of the estimated earnings impact is still an assumption?” [https://marketontology.com](https://marketontology.com?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

comments.author: thinq-81
comments.body: A harder follow-up is “What evidence would weaken the oil-price thesis while the conflict continues?” It forces a distinction between tracking the conflict and tracking the risk you actually own. [https://marketontology.com](https://marketontology.com?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
